html:
The Zapotec are one of the largest Indigenous peoples of Mexico, living mainly in the state of Oaxaca. Ben 'Zaa, Binnizá, Mén Diiste and Bene Xhon are names for themselves in different Zapotec languages, which vary so much from valley to valley that many speakers cannot understand each other.

Their ancestors built Monte Albán, one of the first cities of Mesoamerica, from about 500 BCE, and later towns such as Mitla, famous for its stone fretwork. By 1492 the Zapotec were split among small kingdoms, the later Zapotec states. The lord of Zaachila had moved to the Isthmus of Tehuantepec, where the Zapotec held off an army of the Aztecs at the fortress of Guiengola in the 1490s. Their old rivals were the Mixtec to the north-west.

After the Spanish conquest they kept many of their towns and lands. Benito Juárez, a Zapotec born in 1806, became president of Mexico. The women of the Isthmus are known for their embroidered dress.
